title: NotebookLM: The best use of AI I have found (so far)
author: Craig Barton
summary: Craig Barton reports on Google's NotebookLM as the most useful AI tool he has tried, walking through data extraction from the White Rose Maths PDFs and summarisation of a 41-page Bjork and Soderstrom paper. He stresses the linked references back to the source, the document-limited answers that reduce hallucination, and the one-click podcast that turns a paper into something to listen to on the move. He closes with a caution not to trust output blindly. It is a teacher-facing tool evaluation, with the tool itself as the subject.
points: NotebookLM turned a manual copy-paste-to-Excel job on White Rose small steps into a ten-second prompt.
Numbered references that link each takeaway back to the source passage let a teacher check the claim rather than trust it.
Because the tool only draws on the documents you upload, hallucination risk is lower than with general chatbots, though not zero.
Audio overviews convert dense research papers into podcasts, changing how teachers can consume research.
quotes: However, my new favourite over the last few weeks is NotebookLM from Google. If you need to extract data from documents or are a research geek like me, this will blow your mind.

Until now, I had been manually copying and pasting each of these lists into a text editor (to remove all the formatting) and then into an Excel spreadsheet where I could work on it. This was pretty time-consuming.

If you have ever faced the challenge of extracting the key insights from a lengthy document - perhaps a research paper - then you know how tough it can be. The language may be dry or inaccessible, the signal may be lost amidst the noise, or you don’t have the time required to read, digest and synthesise.

So, at any point, you can dive back into the source material to find the relevant section of the document from which the insight comes. This way, you can check if you agree with the takeaway or delve deeper if you choose.

This opens up a whole new way to consume content. Upload it to NotebookLM, download the podcast you your phone (I use DropBox for this), and listen to it on your travels. It sure beats wading through multiple pages of sometimes unintelligible texts while hunched over your laptop.

And you can upload more than PDF documents. You can upload audio files, link to webpages, or even YouTube videos. And each time NotebookLM will perform the same impressive summarisation functions - podcast included.
